title: ADR-001: PostgreSQL as the system of record
storage:
Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-02-11 · Owners: Platform team

Context

The ledger stores money movements. Every transfer writes at least two entries that must commit together, and finance needs ad-hoc reporting with joins across accounts, entries and settlements.

Decision

We use PostgreSQL as the single system of record for all ledger and account data. We will not introduce MongoDB or any other document database for ledger, transaction or account data.

Alternatives considered

  • MongoDB: rejected. Multi-document transactions exist but are slower and our team has no operational experience with them; schema flexibility is not worth losing strict constraints on money data.
  • DynamoDB: rejected because reporting queries would need a separate analytics copy.

Consequences

Schema changes go through Alembic migrations. Flexible metadata may be stored in a JSONB column instead of a new database.

title: ADR-002: Use SQS for asynchronous jobs, not Kafka
storage:
Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-03-04

Context

We need background processing for webhooks, settlement files and email. We are six engineers with no dedicated ops person.

Decision

We use Amazon SQS queues for asynchronous work. Kafka was rejected: running and upgrading a Kafka cluster is more operational load than a six-person team can carry, and we do not need event replay today.

Revisit when

Revisit if we need ordered event replay across services or exceed 5,000 messages per second.

title: ADR-003: Public partner API is REST with OpenAPI
storage:
Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-04-22

Decision

The public partner API is REST described by an OpenAPI 3.1 spec, versioned in the URL (/v1/). We decided not to offer GraphQL to partners, because per-field authorization and query cost limits are hard to audit for a regulated payments API.

Internal tools may use whatever fits, but anything partners call must be in the OpenAPI spec.

title: ADR-004: Authentication through Auth0 (OIDC)
storage:
Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-05-09

Decision

All user sign-in goes through Auth0 using OIDC. We will not store passwords or build our own login, password reset or MFA flows.

Rationale: SOC 2 scope is smaller when credentials never touch our database, and Auth0 already provides MFA.

title: ADR-005: Frontend server state with TanStack Query
storage:
Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-06-17 · Supersedes the 2025 Redux decision

Decision

New frontend code uses TanStack Query for server state. Redux is superseded and must not be added to new screens; existing Redux slices are migrated when touched.

title: 2026-10-14 Platform sync — meeting notes
storage:
Attendees: Platform team, Payments team

Discussion

  • Settlement job failures last week were caused by retries without idempotency keys.
  • Debate about splitting the ledger service.

Decisions

  • Decision: every endpoint that moves money must require an Idempotency-Key header, and retries must reuse the same key.
  • Decision: no new microservices until the ledger monolith has full test coverage on transfers; new features go into the existing ledger service.

Action items

  • Add idempotency middleware (Payments team).
